text: Why two penguins make same salary,
but one stay poor,
and one become millionaire?
This is Doug.
This is Ricky. Doug brother.
Same job. Same salary.
Both need car.
Doug buy new car. Four thousand four hundred fish.
Doug no have four thousand four hundred fish.
So Doug get loan.
Sixty-five fish every month. Seven years.
Doug happy.
Ricky buy old car. One thousand fish. Cash.
Doug laugh at Ricky car.
But Ricky also take sixty-five fish every month.
Ricky no give fish to bank.
Ricky put fish in stock market.
Doug fish go to bank.
Ricky fish go to work.
Every year, Doug car worth less.
Every year, Ricky fish make baby fish.
Baby fish make more fish.
This is called compound interest.
Doug poor.
In real life, a forty-four thousand dollar car loan for seven years,
is about six hundred fifty dollars a month.
Invest that in stocks, about seven percent a year.
Seven years: seventy thousand dollars.
Thirty-five years: one point one million.
Year seven. Doug make last payment.
Doug car break.
Ricky buy new car. Cash. With baby fish.
Doug buy new car. With new loan.
Team Doug, or team Ricky?
